structure: Article 11.3 and Appendix III plus the 2026–2027 Guide and 18 EC project entry. The chart’s third-year project is verified via its own module and the programme’s graduation section. Seven 6 EC modules plus 9, 6 and 3 in year one. Eight compulsory units and two independently restricted choices of 6 EC each in year two. The open 30 EC, 6 EC methods, 6 EC public communication and 18 EC fieldwork and individual thesis complete year three.
progression: The English and Dutch tracks appear in this order in Article 10.2. The English route is selected on official order. Appendix III and the current course guide establish 60 EC per year, with two separately restricted 6 EC choices in year two and 30 EC of elective space in year three. Article 9.1 sets prior participation in Discovering Anthropology for Global History of Inequality and Ethnographic Research Methodology 1, 90 EC from years one and two for the bachelor project, and project registration for Anthropology for Society. The official project page confirms independent fieldwork and an individual thesis. The programme page identifies three profiles with academic, policy or creative outputs, within the credited curriculum. Separate practical attendance, language diagnostic and first-year study advice rules do not add credits. The Anthropology for Society course specifies completion of project fieldwork before taking it and locates the public-facing profile output in that 6 EC course.
interestAccounting: Two exact-target source blocks of 45 identical themes retain all 90 row IDs. Direct interests and stable directions are addressed or tested, supporting topics contextualize, and examples and career contexts do not generate curricula.
